command: surety session say run_01M53D1HH4F7NGKS00KDF8XCQ7 --project proj_01M53C9CP71558J8MFCQ1NAFER --text Answers: (1) On the incline the block is launched down the slope with kinetic friction only (one μ); it stops at v0²/(2g(μ cos θ − sin θ)) when tan θ < μ, and when tan θ >= μ (including equality, decided within floating-point rounding) it never stops and the lab says so. 'Never stops' is a prediction the player can choose, scored 100 if right and 0 if wrong; a distance predicted for a block that never stops scores 0. (2) The momentum player predicts both carts' velocities after the collision; the lab's score is the mean of the two scores. The trajectory player predicts the range at launch height. (3) For every scored value the relative error's denominator is max(|simulated|, 1 unit), so the 10% band is at least 0.1 m/s or 0.1 m; scores stay unrounded. A relative tolerance on a quantity whose reference is zero (R1.1 with zero total momentum) is measured against Σ|mᵢvᵢ|. (4) Drag acceleration is −k|v|v with k from 0 to 0.5 per metre (1/m); launch and landing at ground level. (5) Carts not approaching each other (v1 <= v2, cart 1 on the left) means no collision and unchanged velocities, reported as such. (6) Add requirements for the input ranges with refusal of out-of-range input, and for the HTTP API (POST /api/momentum and /api/friction answer what the physics modules compute; invalid input gets 400 with a JSON error naming the problem; GET / serves the page), each in the phase of its lab; keep any requirements you already added. Record these, leave no open question, and produce the final product.
